title: Fix it: number the lines of an edi order the way the retailer expects
basics: Inside `map`, `$` is the current element and `$$` is its index, counting from 0. A Number can be written as text with a fixed number of digits using a format pattern: `7 as String {format: "000"}` gives `"007"`.
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

A retailer's EDI system wants every order line numbered, starting at 1, as a three-digit String: `"001"`, `"002"`, and so on.

Given an array of SKUs, return an array of `{ line, sku }`. Orders can have more than nine lines.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
starter:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map { line: "00" ++ ($$ + 1), sku: $ }
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
pads by concatenating "00", so line 10 becomes "0010"
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map { line: ($$ + 1) as String {format: "000"}, sku: $ }

mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map { line: "00" ++ ($$ + 1), sku: $ }

explanation.approach: The index starts at 0, so line numbers are `$$ + 1`. A format pattern of zeros pads to a fixed width whatever the number, whereas gluing a fixed prefix on only works while every number has one digit.

snippets.label: A zero-padded format
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
[1 as String {format: "000"}, 10 as String {format: "000"}]
